title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative: The Federation of Uganda Employers (FUE) adapted its organizational structures and processes in communication and digital strategy in response to changes in the business environment and organizational needs brought on by the COVID 19 pandemic. In March 2020, FUE deployed a recalibrated communication strategy with a newly employed Communication officer. Consequently, FUE made headline news regularly. FUE improved its social media presence by developing a digital strategy in September 2020. Between October 2020 and June 2021, FUE released 32 social media videos; a FUE profile video; 14 videos highlighting FUE impact over the years; 1 expert interview; 2 testimonial videos; and 14 training videos. The digital strategy led to an increase in the number of followers on social media platforms (e.g. Facebook followers saw a tenfold increase by May 2021 compared to 2020). In parallel, FUE increased its visibility with traditional media. FUE organized the first ever media engagement breakfast to present FUE's work (September 2020); conducted 10 press briefings to convey employers' views in 2020-21; and FUE Executive Director had a weekly Op-ed piece in a major journal. Additionally, FUE strengthened communication partnership with trade unions. FUE and National Organisation of Trade Unions (NOTU) issued several joint statements; and hosted webinars on the impact of COVID-19 Pandemic on Employment Relations. FUE signed a tripartite MoU with the Ministry of Labour and NOTU on COVID responses. To enhance communications with members, FUE surveyed members in April 2020 (120 responses) on the impact of COVID-19 on enterprises. Subsequently, FUE provided five guides and two videos on key aspects of managing the COVID 19 crisis. FUE digitalized its training and instituted webinars as a new service offer, which led to a 29% increase in members using online services. Overall FUE increased membership in 2020/21 by 17% and collected more membership subscription as compared to 2019. The ILO established a survey platform that enabled FUE to run 3 enterprise surveys to identify members needs/concerns (between March-Oct 2020). In addition, with the support of the Government of the Netherlands, the ILO assisted with the development of a specific membership survey consisting of 200 qualitative interviews in February 2020. The survey, executed in partnership with UNHCR, targeted growth of FUE in geographical locations where it was weak (Arua and Isingiro districts). With the support of the Government of Switzerland, the ILO commissioned the development FUE's ‘member portal' on the FUE website which enabled FUE to provide advisory services and direct advertising revenue on the website. The ILO supported the development of a digital communications strategy to support a move to an online presence, and supported training to improve the communication skills of FUE staff (three staff communication trainings held between November 2020 and January 2021). The ILO provided FUE with two policy frameworks, one as the pandemic broke to help FUE engage with government and the second at the start of 2021 to support recovery policies. The ILO also commissioned a set of 20 qualitative interviews to support this work (July/August 2021). The ILO developed a digital training platform for FUE, initially to run OSH training courses but this platform was further set up to run a wide range of FUE online training courses. The ILO supported a range of training courses (e.g. labour migration (October 2020), skills anticipation and matching (September 2020), OSH (August-November 2021), membership development (May-June 2020) for FUE (6 staff) to help them throughout the crisis period. The ILO also supported and facilitated a leadership mentor programme for the executive director of FUE (4 coaching sessions with a Top international advocacy expert provided on advocacy and communication strategies).
